el_jadida_page.name: El Jadida
el_jadida_page.hero_subtitle: Atlantic trade winds, UNESCO Portuguese ramparts, a glowing underground cistern and a working harbour of blue fishing boats — the Doukkala coast at its most characterful.

overview.title: Welcome to El Jadida — Portuguese stone on the Atlantic
overview.p1: El Jadida sits on Morocco’s Atlantic Doukkala coast, about an hour south of Casablanca. Its heart is the UNESCO-listed Portuguese City (Mazagan): thick ramparts, the Bastion of the Angel, and the famous underground cistern where a shaft of light falls on still water. With its wide turquoise bay and a horizon where land meets ocean, this coastal town offers the atmosphere of a historic walled city without the intensity of larger tourist hubs.
overview.p2: Beyond the walls: a working fishing port packed with blue boats, the old Jewish Mellah, Medina lanes and souks, the city beach, and the resort strip of Sidi Bouzid with its open Atlantic horizon. This is rocky and sandy Atlantic shore — not desert, not lagoon harbours, not mountain trail country.

places.title: Must-visit places in El Jadida
places.subtitle: Portuguese heritage, harbour life and Atlantic beaches.

citerne.title: Portuguese Cistern
citerne.desc: Vaulted underground reservoir with a single beam of light on the water — the city’s most atmospheric stop.

remparts.title: Ramparts & Bastion of the Angel
remparts.desc: Walk the Portuguese walls for Atlantic views and the iconic sea-facing bastion.

plage.title: El Jadida Beach
plage.desc: City sand and Atlantic swell a short hop from the medina walls.

port.title: Fishing Port
port.desc: Working harbour of blue boats, nets and morning catch.

mellah.title: Old Jewish Mellah
mellah.desc: Historic Jewish quarter lanes within the wider old town fabric.

souks.title: Medina Souks
souks.desc: Everyday markets and narrow streets for spices, produce and local life.

sidi_bouzid.title: Sidi Bouzid
sidi_bouzid.desc: Atlantic resort beach south of town — wider sand and seaside cafés.

cite_portugaise.title: Portuguese City (Mazagan)
cite_portugaise.desc: The fortified ensemble as a whole — gates, walls and the urban core inside.

haouzia.title: Haouzia Coast
haouzia.desc: Coastal stretch and lighthouse moods north of the main resort strip.

transport.title: Getting around
transport.desc: Trains and buses link Casablanca (CMN). Petits taxis cover town, Sidi Bouzid and the station; agree prices for longer coastal hops.

bargain.title: Wind & sun
bargain.desc: Atlantic trade winds can be strong. Bring a layer for the ramparts and high SPF for beach days.

water.title: Tickets & cash
water.desc: The cistern has a small entry fee. Carry dirhams for taxis, port snacks and medina shops.

agadir.title: Sidi Bouzid & Haouzia

q1.question: How many days in El Jadida?
q1.answer: Two days cover the Portuguese City, cistern, ramparts and port. Three days add Sidi Bouzid beach time or a short trip to Azemmour.

q2.question: Is El Jadida only about the Portuguese ruins?
q2.answer: The UNESCO walls and cistern are the headline, but the fishing port, Mellah, souks and Atlantic beaches give a full coastal-town stay.

q3.question: How do I get to El Jadida?
q3.answer: Fly into Casablanca (CMN), then continue by train or road in about an hour. Direct coaches also run from major cities.

q4.question: Best time to visit?
q4.answer: April–June and September–November for milder weather and fewer crowds. Summer is for swimming; winter can be windy and wetter.
